title: PFGateway Health Check Failure
symptoms: HTTP 502/503 responses from gateway endpoint
Health probe returning unhealthy
Traffic Manager routing to single endpoint
High latency on all incoming requests
diagnostic_steps: Check gateway pod status: kubectl get pods -l app=pf-gateway -n pf-system
Review gateway logs for errors: kubectl logs -l app=pf-gateway -n pf-system --tail=200
Verify TLS certificate validity: openssl s_client -connect <gateway-host>:443 -servername <gateway-host> | openssl x509 -noout -dates
Check upstream AAD connectivity: curl -I https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/discovery/v2.0/keys
Inspect Azure Traffic Manager health probe status in Azure Portal
Review Application Insights for failed dependency calls from gateway
mitigation_steps: If certificate expired: renew via Key Vault and restart gateway deployment
If AAD unreachable: initiate cross-region failover via Traffic Manager
If pod is crash-looping: roll back to previous deployment version
If DNS issue: verify AzureDNS zone records and TTL settings
Scale out gateway replicas if CPU/memory is the bottleneck: kubectl scale deployment/pf-gateway --replicas=6

title: PFOrchestrator Unresponsive / High Latency
symptoms: Job submissions timing out
PFOrchestrator health endpoint returning 503 or timing out
Worker pool idle despite jobs in queue
High CPU or memory on orchestrator pods
diagnostic_steps: Check orchestrator pod resource usage: kubectl top pods -l app=pf-orchestrator -n pf-system
Look for OOMKilled events: kubectl describe pod -l app=pf-orchestrator -n pf-system | grep -A10 Events
Check recent deployments: kubectl rollout history deployment/pf-orchestrator -n pf-system
Review orchestrator logs for deadlocks or exceptions: kubectl logs -l app=pf-orchestrator -n pf-system --tail=500
Check PFConfigService health (orchestrator depends on it): curl http://pf-config-service/health
Review distributed traces in Application Insights for slow spans
mitigation_steps: If OOMKilled: roll back to previous version and file memory-leak investigation
If stuck on config: restart PFConfigService first, then PFOrchestrator
If deadlock detected in logs: perform graceful restart: kubectl rollout restart deployment/pf-orchestrator
If recent bad deployment: kubectl rollout undo deployment/pf-orchestrator
Temporarily increase resource limits if load spike: kubectl set resources deployment/pf-orchestrator --limits=memory=4Gi

title: PFStorageService Failures (CosmosDB / Azure Storage)
symptoms: 429 Too Many Requests errors in storage service logs
Job state writes failing
Worker pool unable to read job definitions
CosmosDB latency spike visible in Azure Portal
diagnostic_steps: Check CosmosDB account metrics: Azure Portal > CosmosDB account > Metrics > Request Units
Identify top RU-consuming queries: Azure Portal > CosmosDB > Insights > Top 10 Requests
Check for long-running batch jobs: kubectl get jobs -n pf-jobs
Review storage service logs: kubectl logs -l app=pf-storage-service -n pf-system --tail=200
Check Azure Storage account status at https://status.azure.com
Verify Key Vault connectivity for storage credentials: kubectl exec -it <pod> -- curl http://169.254.169.254/metadata/identity/oauth2/token
mitigation_steps: If RU exhaustion: identify and pause offending batch jobs, then scale up throughput
If Azure Storage outage: activate secondary storage account failover
If Key Vault unreachable: ensure MSI role assignments are correct, restart pods
Scale up CosmosDB throughput temporarily: az cosmosdb sql container throughput update --throughput 50000
Enable request throttling on the storage service to protect CosmosDB
escalation_path: PF-Storage-DRI -> Azure CosmosDB Support -> Azure Storage Support

title: PFWorkerPool Job Processing Failures
symptoms: Jobs stuck in 'Queued' state for > 5 minutes
Worker pods showing high error rate
Service Bus queue depth growing without drain
PFResultCollector reporting no results received
diagnostic_steps: Check worker pod logs: kubectl logs -l app=pf-worker-pool -n pf-system --tail=300
Inspect Service Bus queue metrics: az servicebus queue show --name pf-jobs --namespace-name <ns>
Check dead-letter queue depth: az servicebus queue show --name pf-jobs/$deadletterqueue --namespace-name <ns>
Verify PFStorageService is healthy: curl http://pf-storage-service/health
Check for node-level issues: kubectl describe nodes | grep -A5 'Conditions'
Review recent config changes that may affect worker processing logic
mitigation_steps: If Service Bus is full: purge dead-letter queue and restart workers
If PFStorage is unhealthy: fix storage first (see TSG-003), then restart workers
Scale out worker pool for capacity issues: kubectl scale deployment/pf-worker-pool --replicas=20
Restart worker pool to clear stuck state: kubectl rollout restart deployment/pf-worker-pool
If node issues: cordon and drain the problematic node, let scheduler move pods

title: Cross-Cluster Communication Failure
symptoms: Requests from West US cluster failing to reach East US cluster
Traffic Manager health probe failures on one endpoint
Increased latency for cross-region API calls
Network policy errors in pod logs
diagnostic_steps: Check Traffic Manager endpoint health: az traffic-manager endpoint show --profile-name pf-traffic-manager
Verify VNet peering status: az network vnet peering list --resource-group <rg> --vnet-name <vnet>
Test cross-cluster connectivity: kubectl exec -it <pod> -- curl -v http://pf-gateway.pf-cluster-westus.svc.cluster.local/health
Check Network Security Group rules for inter-cluster ports
Review PFLoadBalancer logs for failed backend connections
Check Azure ExpressRoute or VPN Gateway status if applicable
mitigation_steps: If Traffic Manager probe failing: update probe health thresholds or failover to healthy endpoint
If VNet peering broken: re-establish peering connection via Azure Portal
If NSG blocking traffic: add allow rule for required ports (443, 8080, 9090)
Route all traffic to single healthy cluster until cross-cluster link is restored
Engage Azure Networking team if infrastructure-level issue suspected

title: PFAlertingService Not Firing Incidents
symptoms: Known outage with no ICM incident created
PagerDuty not receiving alerts
Azure Monitor alert rules showing 'No data'
Health probe metrics gap in dashboards
diagnostic_steps: Check Azure Monitor alert rule status in Azure Portal
Verify PFHealthProbe is running: kubectl get pods -l app=pf-health-probe -n pf-system
Check PFMetricsEmitter logs: kubectl logs -l app=pf-metrics-emitter -n pf-system --tail=100
Verify Azure Monitor workspace connectivity from pods
Check PagerDuty integration webhook in Azure Monitor action groups
Review ICM connector configuration and credentials
mitigation_steps: Manually create ICM incident if alerting is down
Restart PFHealthProbe and PFMetricsEmitter
Validate Azure Monitor workspace ingestion via Log Analytics query
Re-configure action group webhook if PagerDuty token has rotated
Use Azure CLI to manually trigger test alert: az monitor metrics alert create (test rule)
